Check latest updates for Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Odisha & Chhattisgarh as IMD issues heavy rain alerts By Trending Desk , ET Online Last Updated: Nov 03, 2026, 12:05:00 AM IST Rate Story Follow us Share Font Size Abc Small Abc Medium Abc Large Save Print Comment Synopsis School holiday November 3: Cyclone Murasu has led to school closures in several districts of Andhra Pradesh and Odisha. Nellore, Prakasam and Palnadu in Andhra Pradesh, as well as Kandhamal and Rayagada in Odisha, have declared holidays for November 3. Schools in Malkangiri will remain shut until November 4. Here are the latest updates from Tamil Nadu too.

 ET Online School Holiday Update Schools in several districts of Andhra Pradesh and Odisha will remain closed on Tuesday, November 3, as Severe Cyclonic Storm Murasu approaches the east coast. District administrations have announced precautionary holidays in areas expected to experience heavy rainfall and strong winds. In Andhra Pradesh, holidays have been announced in Nellore and Prakasam, among other affected districts. In Odisha, Kandhamal and Rayagada have also ordered educational institutions to remain shut on November 3 and 4. Malkangiri has announced a longer closure from November 2 to 4.
 In Tamil Nadu, schools and colleges in Chennai and Tiruvallur remained closed on November 2 due to the storm. However, no official confirmation of a holiday in these districts for November 3 was available in the latest updates. Students and parents are advised to check with their schools and respective district administrations for further announcements.
 Read the IMD's full weather alert HERE 
 Andhra Pradesh school holiday update: Will schools be closed today?
Andhra Pradesh is expected to bear the brunt of Cyclone Murasu, with the IMD forecasting heavy to extremely heavy rainfall and strong winds in several districts.
According to reports, Nellore and Prakasam district administrations have declared a holiday on November 3 for government, private and aided schools, Anganwadi centres, and government and private junior colleges. Palnadu district has also announced a holiday for schools, colleges and Anganwadi centres as a precautionary measure.
 Live Events
 The IMD has forecast wind speeds of 100–110 kmph, with gusts reaching 120 kmph during landfall. The cyclone is expected to cross the south Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Narsapur, south of Ongole, around midnight on November 2 or in the early hours of November 3.
 Other districts are also under weather alerts. However, a rain warning does not automatically mean schools are closed. Parents should check the latest orders issued by their district Collectors.
 Odisha school holiday update: Will schools remain closed on November 3?
Several districts in Odisha have declared school holidays as a precautionary measure amid the threat posed by Cyclone Murasu.
Kandhamal: All schools will remain closed on November 3 and 4. The order covers students up to Class 12. Scheduled examinations and other academic activities will not be affected, according to the district administration.
Rayagada: All government, aided and private educational institutions will remain closed on November 3 and 4.
Malkangiri: Schools, colleges and Anganwadi centres will remain closed from November 2 to 4.
The IMD has forecast rainfall and strong winds in southern Odisha districts, including Malkangiri, Koraput, Rayagada, Gajapati and Ganjam. Residents have been advised to follow instructions issued by local authorities.
 Tamil Nadu school holiday update: Chennai and nearby districts on alert
Tamil Nadu, especially its northern districts, is also likely to experience bad weather as Cyclone Murasu moves towards the Andhra Pradesh coast.
The weather department has issued a wind warning for Chennai, Thiruvallur, Ranipet, Kancheepuram and Chengalpattu districts, along with the Puducherry coast.
Wind speeds of 50-60 kmph, with gusts reaching 70 kmph, are prevailing in these areas. They may increase to 60-70 kmph, with gusts reaching 80 kmph, until the early hours of November 3.
Chennai and nearby districts will remain on alert as the storm approaches. Parents should check with local authorities and schools for any holiday announcements.
 Cyclone Murasu latest update: What has IMD said?
The cyclone is being monitored by Doppler Weather Radars at Chennai and Machilipatnam. With heavy rainfall and strong winds expected in parts of Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and Tamil Nadu, more school holiday announcements may follow. Students and parents should keep checking official district updates for the latest information.
 Disclaimer: This article is based on information available at the time of writing. Readers are advised to check official announcements for the latest updates.
